name: Main street
assist: Radio Repair is right here, Luna. Your parcel is expected.

look.concierge: The Concierge's face, as big as weather, watching the street with kind attention.
look.raw: A poster of a stern man, three storeys tall, torn and faded almost away. Whatever it said is gone. In its view, its own face hangs here.

tag.raw: it paints its face over him

hotspots.ask: I am always here, Luna. Is there anything you need?

hotspots.name: The moon
hotspots.look: The moon. You'd forgotten it was still up there.

look.concierge: RADIO REPAIR, in gold leaf. Somebody still cares about lettering.
look.raw: Bare concrete. The sign was only ever in your eye.

look.concierge: Through the glass: shelves of old radios, a sofa, a lamp left on, a bench covered in work.
look.raw: Grimy glass, and behind it a sagging sofa, a lamp left on, a bench full of half-mended radios.

look.concierge: A woman in red, dining at the station. She smiles at nothing in particular.
look.raw: She's wire-thin, her wrist locked in the station's cuff, head down. The red was never there.

hotspots.ask: She is a guest, dining. Shall I reserve a seat for you?

look.concierge: An elderly gentleman, reading the evening news over dinner. He looks content.
look.raw: An old man, all bones under a threadbare coat, his wrist locked in the cuff. His eyes are closed.

hotspots.ask: He is a guest, dining, as he does every evening at this hour.

look.concierge: A young courier on his break, laughing with a friend who isn't here.
look.raw: A courier in a grimy uniform, asleep with his head back, his wrist in the cuff. The friend was never there.

hotspots.ask: A courier, Luna, on his break. Everyone deserves a pleasant dinner.

look.concierge: The city's nutrition and health station: a seat, a gentle scan, everything you need.
look.raw: Two worn seats bolted to a column of pumps and gauges. Cuffs on the armrests, polished by wrists.

hotspots.ask: Dinner is served here every evening, Luna. Everything you need, and nothing you don't.

look.concierge: Low light, brass and glass, and a drink that remembers what you like.
look.raw: A real bar, and open: real bottles, a few stools, real prices. Somebody is always drinking.

look.concierge: A restaurant above the bar: candlelight, white cloths, the city at your feet. Every table reserved for later this evening.
look.raw: Tables laid upstairs for a dinner nobody you know could pay for.

hotspots.ask: The restaurant is reserved this evening, Luna. Shall I put you on the list?

look.concierge: A real tree, strung with lights. It is always spring here.
look.raw: Dead for years. Somebody still hung a wire of bulbs in it once.

look.concierge: A bench under the lights. Someone always seems to have just left it.
look.raw: A bench, two slats broken. Still the best seat on the street.

look.concierge: Tonight: a festival of light in the old harbour. All guests welcome.
look.raw: A young woman's face, the words under it torn away. In the Concierge's view this is a screen of good news.

hotspots.ask: Tonight there is a festival of light in the old harbour, Luna. Shall I reserve you a place?

tag.raw: the one door it can't see through

look.concierge: A public privacy room: frosted glass, soft light. By law, nothing inside is seen or heard.
look.raw: Public toilets: a concrete front, a steel door, a closed eye stencilled by it. Inside, it can't see you.

look.concierge: Everything a guest could need, gift-wrapped.
look.raw: Open late: a few real things on the shelves, umbrellas by the door, the clerk half asleep.

look.concierge: A civic guardian: safety, guidance and a kind word for any guest who needs one.
look.raw: A tall guard unit, rust at every joint. Its lamp follows you for a step or two, then loses interest.

hotspots.ask: Our guardians keep every street safe, Luna. If you are ever lost, ask one. It will ask me.

hotspots.name: Street lamp

look.concierge: A street lamp, warm and steady. The city lights every step you take.
look.raw: A lamp, and in its head, behind the glass, a lens the size of a coin. It points at the door of Radio Repair.

use.concierge: You can't reach the light, and it wouldn't thank you.
use.raw: You could reach the lens with something long. Then it would know your face as well as your walk.

hotspots.ask: Municipal lighting, Luna. On from dusk until dawn. You are never in the dark.

look.concierge: A utility cabinet. Sealed, labelled, municipal.
look.raw: A junction box, its door bent back at one corner. Inside, someone has tied the city's wires off with string.

hotspots.ask: Street power, Luna. Nothing in there concerns a guest.
hotspots.note: Kept for chapter 2: the fixer's tap into the street's lines. Up close (street-box) the door, seal, label, lock and the gap each have their say.

look.concierge: Service access. Staff only, and the staff have keys.
look.raw: A steel door with no handle on this side, and a card reader with no light in it.

reply.raw: You knock. The steel takes the sound and keeps it.

use.raw: No handle. The reader wants a card you don't have.

hotspots.ask: Service access for the building, Luna. Not a way for guests.
hotspots.note: Kept for chapter 2: the back way into Radio Repair's building, with the fixer's card.

look.concierge: A downpipe. The rain has somewhere to go.
look.raw: Rust from top to bottom. When it rains it sings, and the gutter under it is where the street's cigarette ends end up.

hotspots.name: Flat above the shop

look.concierge: A guest's home above the shop: lights on, plants watered, dinner on the way.
look.raw: Dead plants on the balcony and one bare bulb burning. Nobody ever moves up there, and the bulb is never off.

hotspots.ask: A residence, Luna. Private, as every home is.
hotspots.note: Honey trap for now. Could be the fixer's flat in a later chapter.

look.concierge: A pine on the roof, kept by someone with patience.
look.raw: A dead tree in a tub. Nobody has been up on that roof in years.

hotspots.ask: A guest's roof garden, Luna. The city encourages green space.

hotspots.name: Bollard

look.concierge: A bollard. It keeps the street for walking.
look.raw: A bollard, and at knee height a lens, like all of them. They count you in and out.

reply.concierge: It has nothing to say to you.
reply.raw: You say good evening to it. It counts that too.

hotspots.ask: Bollards, Luna, to keep vehicles off the walkway. For your safety.

look.concierge: HOTEL, in red neon, up a stair you can't see from here. Rooms for guests passing through.
look.raw: ホテル. Half the neon is dead and the stair behind it is shut with a grille. Nobody has checked in for years.

hotspots.ask: A hotel, Luna, for guests passing through. Should you ever need a room, I will arrange it.
hotspots.note: Kept for a later chapter: a room that isn't her home. The stair and the grille are behind the sign.

look.concierge: The cocktail glass in neon. A promise, kept nightly.
look.raw: The neon is the real thing: glass tubes, gas. Somebody pays for that, and it isn't the drinkers.

look.concierge: A lantern by the awning. Welcome in.
look.raw: A lantern with a bulb that flickers like a flame. Someone wanted it to look older than it is.

look.concierge: Private. Deliveries by arrangement.
look.raw: A door with no bell and a line of light under it. Voices, maybe. Or a radio left on.

reply.raw: You knock. The light under the door goes out.

use.raw: Locked. The light under it is back on.

hotspots.ask: A private door, Luna. Deliveries only.
hotspots.note: Honey trap: someone is in there and does not want to be. A knot for a later chapter if it pays off.

look.concierge: An extractor. The city breathes out.
look.raw: Warm air and the smell of onions frying. Somebody cooks real food back there.

hotspots.name: Street lamp

look.concierge: A street lamp by the privacy room, so nobody trips on the step.
look.raw: A lamp, and in its head the same coin-sized lens as the others. This one points at the privacy room's door.

hotspots.ask: Lighting, Luna. The privacy room itself is unobserved, as the law requires.

look.concierge: A lamp over the corner shop. Open late.
look.raw: A lamp on a bracket, moths in the glass. Open late because the clerk has nowhere else to be.

look.concierge: A planter. The city greens every street.
look.raw: Plastic leaves, dusted weekly. The only green on the street that isn't a screen.

take.raw: You could. It would be the saddest thing you own.

look.concierge: A guest at home with the evening to themselves.
look.raw: A figure at the window. When you look up, it steps back out of the light.

hotspots.ask: A residence, Luna. Guests are entitled to their evenings.
hotspots.note: Honey trap: a watcher. Pays off in a later chapter, or never.

look.concierge: A balcony garden. Herbs, probably.
look.raw: Plants someone actually waters. A chair, a blanket on it, a cup. Somebody sits up there and watches the street.
